knowledgePoint.title: Solving Rational Equations with a Binomial in One Denominator

response.solution:
First, we note that $x=-3$ cannot be a solution since this would make the denominator on the right-hand side zero.

We can flip an equation involving two fractions as follows:

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}\,⟹\,\frac{b}{a}=\frac{d}{c}
$$

The above technique works whenever $a$ and $c$ are both different from zero.

Therefore, we can flip the given equation as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{2}=\frac{x+3}{7}
$$

We can now solve this equation using the addition and the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{x+3}{7} \\ 7\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) & =7\cdot \left(\frac{x+3}{7}\right) \\ \frac{7}{2} & =\cancel{7}\cdot \left(\frac{x+3}{\cancel{7}}\right) \\ \frac{7}{2} & =x+3 \\ \frac{7}{2}-3 & =x+3-3 \\ \frac{1}{2} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the solution is $x=\frac{1}{2}.$
